The deal combines two major Appalachian Basin producers, giving EQT greater scale and infrastructure to serve utilities, LNG ​exporters and industrial customers.

Including debt, the combined company will have an enterprise value of more than $50 ​billion.

US natural gas consumption is expected to hit record highs, driven by LNG exports and ⁠power demand from AI data centers.

The Energy Information Administration forecasts domestic consumption to rise from 91.9 billion ​cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 94.3 bcfd in 2027.

EQT now expects potential Appalachian gas demand rising to ​25 bcfd, compared with its previous estimate of 20 bcfd, CEO Toby Rice said on a conference call.

The combined company will have net production of more than 9 billion cubic feet equivalent per day (bcfed), over 30 years of drilling inventory across nearly ​3 million net acres and more than 3,700 miles of midstream infrastructure.

Range shareholders will receive 0.987 EQT shares per share held, valuing ‌the deal ⁠at $12.83 billion, or $54.91 per share, a 20.6% premium to Friday's closing price, according to a Reuters calculation.

Shares of EQT fell 3.7%, while those of Range Resources jumped 15.1% at $52.43.

EQT shareholders will own about 73% of the combined company, while Range investors will hold the remaining 27%. The transaction is expected to close in the first ​quarter of 2027.

The combined company ​expects to generate about $20 ⁠billion in cumulative free cash flow over five years at recent market prices.

William Blair analyst Bert Donnes said the deal strengthened EQT's standing as a leading ​supplier into growing gas and power markets and positioned the company to benefit from ​an eventual ⁠rebound in natural gas prices.

The deal is also expected to lower EQT's unlevered free cash flow breakeven to below $2 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), helping it remain profitable through swings in natural gas prices.

Rice said future production growth would ⁠be ​driven by customer demand rather than output targets, adding that mid-single-digit ​growth was achievable.

EQT's management team will lead the combined company, which will retain its headquarters in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania.

Two Range representatives, including CEO Dennis ​Degner, will join EQT's board.
